title: Consumer AI Age Verification & Legal Basis Gate Pattern
description: A pattern requiring a documented GDPR legal basis, published privacy notice, and effective age-verification mechanism before a consumer AI product is made available to EU users, rather than launching first and addressing compliance reactively.

history.note: Normalized title to match the dataset's 'ends with Pattern' naming convention, reordered for grammatical clarity (was "Age Verification & Legal Basis Gate for Consumer AI").

problem: Consumer AI products, particularly conversational or companion-style products, are often launched globally without first confirming a GDPR legal basis for processing EU users' data or verifying that users below a product's stated minimum age are actually excluded.
solution: Before EU launch, document the specific legal basis relied on for each category of processing (including any use of user interactions for model training), publish a privacy notice in plain language, and implement an age-verification step stronger than a self-reported checkbox for any product that could plausibly be used by minors.
applicability: Any consumer-facing generative AI or AI companion product available to EU users, particularly products with emotionally engaging or companion-style interaction design.
consequences: Effective age verification is a genuinely hard problem (most methods are either weak or privacy-invasive); documenting a legal basis for training-data use may constrain which data can be used for model improvement.

citations.title: Intelligenza artificiale, dal Garante privacy stop al chatbot 'Replika'. Troppi i rischi per i minori e le persone emotivamente fragili
citations.publisher: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali

relationships.reason: A documented legal basis and privacy notice are the concrete mechanism satisfying this control.
The pattern's output feeds the same data protection impact assessment evidence type used elsewhere for GDPR-triggering processing.
